items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the retirement and social security law, in relation to the
ordinary death benefit
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6619

SPONSOR: GOUNARDES
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the retirement and social security law, in relation to
the ordinary death benefit

 
PURPOSE:

This legislation increases the age at which the ordinary death benefit
commences to be reduced while a member of the New York State and Local
Retirement System (NYSLRS) is in service to the full retirement age.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of this bill amends the closing paragraph of paragraph 2 of
subdivision a of section 448 of the retirement and social security law
to amend the date the ordinary death benefit begins to be reduced for
NYSLRS members.

Section 2 of the bill amends the closing paragraph of paragraph 2 of
subdivision a of section 508 of the retirement and social security law
to amend the date the ordinary death benefit begins to be reduced for
NYSLRS members.

Section 3 of the bill amends the closing subparagraph of paragraph 2 of
subdivision a of section 606 of the retirement and social security law
to amend the date the ordinary death benefit begins to be reduced for
NYSLRS members.

Section 4 of this bill states that the provisions of this bill shall not
be subject to section 25 of the retirement and social security law.

Section 5 establishes an effective date of the first of April next
succeeding the date on which it shall have become a law. April first is
the first day of NYSLRS' fiscal year.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Most members of the New York State and Local Retirement System who die
while in active service are covered by an ordinary death benefit equal
to a member's salary multiplied by his or her full years of service
credit, not to exceed three years' salary.  NYSLRS is made up of both
the New York State and Local Employees' Retirement System (ERS) and the
New York State and Local Police and Fire Retirement System (PFRS).
Currently, if a member is still in service at age 61, state law requires
NYSLRS to reduce this Ordinary Death Benefit payable by 4 percent per
year, but it cannot be reduced below 60 percent of the original benefit
payable. This bill increases the age at which the ordinary death benefit
commences to be reduced while a member is in service from age 61 to age
62 for these NYSLRS members in Tiers 2 through 5 and from age 61 to age
63 for Tier 6 NYSLRS members. The rationale for this bill is that the
full retirement age for these NYSLRS members with less than 30 years of
service in Tiers 2 through 6 is age 62. It was increased to age 63 for
Tier 6 members. These members and their beneficiaries should not be
penalized for the fact that they are continuing to work up to the date
that they are first eligible for retirement without incurring an early
retirement penalty. It should be noted that the full retirement age for
Social Security has steadily increased since the 1980's resulting in
more members delaying retirement until they reach their full retirement
age in Social Security; those born from 1960 on reach full retirement
age for Social Security at 67.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

None

 
FISCAL IMPLICATION:

Insofar as this bill affects the ERS, if this legislation is enacted
during the 2021 legislative session, there would be an increase in the
present value of future costs of approximately $19.4 million which would
be shared by the State of New York and all of the participating employ-
ers in the ERS. The estimated first year cost would be approximately
$954,000 to the State of New York and approximately $1.37 million to the
participating employers in the ERS. Insofar as this bill affects PFRS,
if this legislation is enacted during the 2021 legislative session, we
anticipate that the cost will be negligible.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the first of April next succeeding the
date on which it shall have become a law.

summary: Delays reductions in the ordinary death benefit payable to members of the New York State and Local Retirement and the New York State and Local Police and Fire Retirement System to ensure that no reduction before a member becomes retirement eligible for an unreduced retirement from age 61 to 62 for members in Tiers 1-5 and 63 for members in Tier 6.
